goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/authorization/AdminPermissionsSchema.java:226 — Existing admin-permissions clients are returned before the new Clients resource, its scopes, and its all-resource entry are added, so upgraded realms cannot use the newly exposed authorization-schema contract.

adjudication.rationale: The finding references line 226 in AdminPermissionsSchema.java, but the diff only shows changes up to around line 188. The diff shows the CLIENTS resource type being properly added to the schema Map in the constructor (line 72), and the resolveClient method being added. There is no evidence in the diff of any migration or upgrade logic that would cause existing admin-permissions clients to miss the new Clients resource. The finding appears to reference code or behavior not present in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:87 — Global manage permission is omitted from canView(), so a caller granted manage on all clients cannot pass canList() to list them.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at ClientPermissionsV2.java, the canView() method at line 85-87 is: `public boolean canView() { return canViewClientDefault() || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW); }`. It only checks for VIEW permission, not MANAGE. However, canManage() at line 72-75 checks for MANAGE permission. The canList() method (inherited from ClientPermissions) likely calls canView(). If a user has global MANAGE permission on all clients, they should also be able to view/list them, but canView() doesn't include hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). Compare this to canView(ClientScopeModel) at lines 113-116 which correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE: `return hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW) || hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. This inconsistency suggests the finding is valid - canView() should also check for MANAGE permission.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:260 — The tests never exercise the new map-roles-client-scope grant or its deny path, so regressions in ClientPermissionsV2.canMapClientScopeRoles remain undetected.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE as a new scope in AdminPermissionsSchema and implements canMapClientScopeRoles() in ClientPermissionsV2.java. The test file PermissionClientTest.java at line 260 tests MAP_ROLES and MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE but does not include MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE in the createPermission call or verify its behavior. This is a valid observation that the new canMapClientScopeRoles functionality lacks test coverage, which is an important non-bug issue for newly added logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java:126 — Client resource permission tests only use the internal client ID and omit the new clientId fallback in resolveClient, leaving that externally accepted identifier path unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new `resolveClient` method in AdminPermissionsSchema.java (lines 175-183) has a fallback path that first tries `getClientById` and then falls back to `getClientByClientId`. However, examining the test file PermissionClientTest.java, all tests use `myclient.getId()` (the internal UUID) when creating permissions, never testing with the clientId string (like 'myclient'). This means the `getClientByClientId` fallback path in resolveClient is not covered by tests. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly added logic, not a bug in the code itself.
